h: Mourning Gives Way to the Temple’s Joy on Shabbos

p: כׇּל ו׳ הַנֶּחָמוֹת עַד שַׁבָּת זֶה
All six consolations up to this Shabbos
הָיוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְנַחֵם אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
כְּמוֹ נַחֲמוּ נַחֲמוּ עַמִּי (יְשַׁעְיָה מ, א)
וְכֵן קוּמִי אוֹרִי כִּי בָא אוֹרֵךְ (שָׁם ס, א)
and likewise "Arise, shine, for your light has come" (Yeshayahu 60:1),
But the consolation of this Shabbos,
which corresponds to the middah of Malchus:
And this is why the haftarah begins (Yeshayahu 61:10):
and among them were the Tannaim
and the Amoraim and the Rishonim,
and when did they see her joy?
And if it means after the Resurrection of the Dead,
except one who denied the Resurrection of the Dead,
and then all will see her joy.
it is as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days;
de'ah was placed between two Names,
Mikdash was placed between two Names."
That is, being surrounded between two Names
indicates being surrounded entirely by holiness;
לָכֵן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הוּא אוֹר מַקִּיף
therefore the Beis HaMikdash is a surrounding light,
which is the inwardness of Kesser Elyon,
וְכֶתֶר הוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינַת אוֹר מַקִּיף
and Kesser is also the aspect of a surrounding light.
וְזֶהוּ כְּעֵין שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עַל לֶעָתִיד (יְשַׁעְיָה נב, יב)
And this is like what is said of the future (Yeshayahu 52:12):
and the God of Yisrael is your rear guard,"
like "the rear guard of all the camps";
that is, Hashem Yisbarach goes before you
which is a surrounding light from every side.
וּבְמִזְמוֹר שֶׁל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים צב, יד)
And in the Psalm of the Shabbos day it is written (Tehillim 92:14):
in the courtyards of our God";
for on Shabbos there is the spreading of the shelter of peace
over us and over all Yisrael;
the aspect of the surrounding light shines,
is like the Mikdash in space.
And then every one of Yisrael feels
as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days.
וְאָז הוּא בִּבְחִינַת שׂוֹשׂ אָשִׂישׂ בַּה׳
And then he is in the aspect of "I will greatly rejoice in Hashem,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קלג, א)
it is said of the Ancient of Days,
for He is the joy of all."
And at the second meal of Shabbos,
which is the meal of Atika,
and likewise at all the meals of Shabbos,
then the Jew feels the joy,
as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days,
that he is surrounded by holiness on every side,
and he is "in the courtyards of My holiness."
And this is what is said:

p: אָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָּתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן (בְּרָכוֹת מב, ב)
a person fixes his meal over wine (Berachos 42b),
which is like what is said (Yeshayahu 62:9):
"And those who gather it will drink it
in the courtyards of My holiness."
For of wine it is stated (Yoma 76b):
"If he is worthy, he becomes a head;
if he is not worthy, he becomes poor";
and likewise, "if he is worthy, it gladdens him;
if he is not worthy, it desolates him."
And on Shabbos, which is the aspect of "in the courtyards of My holiness,"
then "those who gather it will drink it,"
for then it is in the aspect of "if he is worthy, it gladdens him."
And this is why we say at the second meal:
דְּדַעַת הוּא רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ (רַשִׁ״י פָּרָשַׁת תִּשָּׂא)
for Daas is Ruach HaKodesh (Rashi, Parshas Ki Sisa),
and it is the aspect of the first light
the aspect of "if he is worthy, it gladdens him,"
and this is "I will greatly rejoice in Hashem,"
"My soul shall exult in my God":
for the main thing is the soul,
while the body is called "the flesh of man,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב עו, א)
as is written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 76a).
And therefore the consolation is said on Shabbos,
for then one is in the aspect of "a tzaddik," etc.,
"in the courtyards of our God they will flourish" (Tehillim 92:13–14),
as if the Beis HaMikdash were built in his days.
